Cross-checked with api.nhtsa.gov/SafetyRatings/VehicleId/19595: RolloverPossibility 0.095, dynamicTipResult 'No Tip'. Evidence quotes are 'FIELD = value' pairs from the CSV row.

mass.curb_mass.description: Curb mass (manufacturer curb weight), 2024 Sport Touring hatchback 6MT

candidates.locator: DIMENSIONS table, row 'Curb weight – MT/CVT (kg)', SPORT TOURING column
candidates.notes: Canadian figure for exactly the target trim and gearbox. Columns are SPORT then SPORT TOURING; Sport is CVT-only in Canada for 2024 (NA for MT). The resolver selects the Canadian record.

candidates.locator: Exterior Measurements table, row 'Curb Weight (6MT/CVT)', Sport Touring column
candidates.evidence: Curb Weight (6MT/CVT) NA / 2877 lbs 2932 lbs / 2956 lbs NA / 3053 lbs 3036 lbs / 3102 lbs
candidates.notes: US figure for the same trim/gearbox; 3036 lb = 1377.1 kg, about 5 kg below the Canadian 1382 kg. The difference is small (0.4 %) and may come from Canadian-market equipment or rounding/definition differences; both are kept, the Canadian value is the target-market value.

candidates.locator: WEIGHT section, row 'Curb Weight (lbs.) (6MT)', 4th column (Sport Touring)
candidates.notes: Independent Honda press document agreeing with hondainfocenter (3036 lb).

candidates.locator: DIMENSIONS table, row 'Curb weight (kg) MT/CVT', Sport Touring column
candidates.notes: Model-year check: identical to 2024 (1382 kg).

candidates.locator: DIMENSIONS table, row 'Curb weight (kg) MT/CVT', Sport Touring column
candidates.notes: Model-year check: identical to 2023 and 2024 (1382 kg).

mass.front_fraction.description: Static front-axle share of curb mass

candidates.locator: Exterior Measurements table, row 'Weight Distribution (front/rear, 6MT)', Sport Touring column (4th)
candidates.notes: Published to whole percent, so the true value lies in about 0.585-0.595. The two printed values sit in the Sport (60/40) and Sport Touring (59/41) columns; LX and EX-L cells are empty (no 6MT), checked in raw HTML. US-market figure; no Canadian distribution figure found (Honda Canada spec release lists none). Same trim/gearbox/body/engine, so mechanically applicable to the Canadian car (CA curb mass differs by ~5 kg).

candidates.locator: WEIGHT section, row 'Weight Distribution (%) (front/rear) (6MT)', 4th column (Sport Touring)
candidates.notes: Second Honda document, same 59/41 to whole percent.

candidates.locator: EXTERIOR MEASUREMENTS, row 'Weight Distribution (front/rear, 6MT)', Sport Touring column
candidates.notes: Also on hondainfocenter.com 2022 specs (cache/pages/ff52eae8cd7d0fc1.txt, column 4 = Sport Touring checked in HTML).
candidates.selection_reason: Same value as the 2024 figure (59 %) printed to one more decimal; curb weight is unchanged 2022-2024 (US 3036 lb, CA 1382 kg), so the 2022 decimal figure is the most precise applicable value.

candidates.notes: Same value in both Canadian trim columns.

candidates.locator: EPA Mileage Ratings / Fuel table, row 'Fuel Tank Capacity'
candidates.evidence: Fuel Tank Capacity 12.39 gal 12.39 gal 12.39 gal 12.39 gal
candidates.notes: 12.39 US gal = 46.9 L; Canada prints 46 L. Same tank, different rounding/unit convention (not a conflict beyond rounding: 46 L as printed vs 46.9 L).
Rounded version of 12.39 gal.

candidates.evidence: The specific gravity of gasoline ranges from 0.71 to 0.77 … Finished marketable gasoline is traded (in Europe) with a standard reference of 0.755 kilograms per liter

applicability.notes: generic gasoline, not Canadian regular specifically

candidates.how_to_measure: Hydrometer on a sample of the fuel actually used (Canadian regular, summer/winter blend), at 15 C.
candidates.notes: Value 755 kg/m3 = 0.755 kg/L as printed (unit change only); range from specific gravity 0.71-0.77. Canadian winter blends are at the light end.

mass.fuel_level_assumed.description: Fuel fill fraction included in the published curb mass

candidates.evidence: Curb weight means the weight of a motor vehicle with standard equipment; maximum capacity of engine fuel, oil, and coolant
candidates.how_to_measure: Weigh the car on four corner scales with a full tank (filled to first click) and again near empty; the difference over 46 L fuel mass confirms the convention.
candidates.notes: Honda does not state its curb-weight definition on the spec pages opened; applying the US FMVSS definition (full tank) is an inference, hence class E. No Canadian definition found on the Honda Canada spec release.

mass.ssf_nhtsa.description: NHTSA measured Static Stability Factor, T/(2h)

candidates.locator: Safercar_data.csv, row HONDA / CIVIC HATCHBACK / 2024 / 5 HB / FWD, field STATIC_STABI_FACTOR

applicability.notes: NHTSA lists one SSF for the whole 2022-2024 Civic family; test vehicle not identified (crash-test VINs in row are 2022 Civic Sedans).

candidates.notes: Government measurement, but probably on a Civic Sedan (same platform; hatch differs in rear body, ST trim has 18 in wheels). Printed to 0.01, i.e. 1.475-1.485. Used by derivation mass.cg_height.

candidates.how_to_measure: Four-pad corner scales, full tank, no driver, tyres at placard pressure, level floor; record each corner ±1 kg.
candidates.notes: Left/right split unknown; a lateral CG offset of a few mm is expected (driver-side steering column, battery position) but is unpublished.
searches: Honda spec releases give only axle split (59.1/40.9)
no instrumented test with corner weights found in time budget

candidates.how_to_measure: Weigh wheel+tyre, rotor, caliper, knuckle/hub during a brake or strut job; add half of strut, driveshaft and control arm masses.
searches: no published part masses for knuckle/hub/brake/strut found; parts-catalog shipping weights are not part masses

candidates.how_to_measure: Weigh wheel+tyre, rotor, caliper, hub/knuckle; add half of link, damper and spring masses.
searches: no published rear multi-link component masses found

candidates.how_to_measure: Corner scales: x_cg = (T/2)*((FR+RR)-(FL+RL))/m using front/rear tracks per axle.
candidates.notes: Taken as the centreline: the body is symmetric and no lateral split is published. Range allows for driver-side column/pedal box and the battery; a measured left/right split replaces it.
